chapter_title: AI Agents, Prompts, and Rubric Scoring
learning_objective: The learner will judge whether each of ten rubric checks should be done by a tool, by the model, or by a person, with at least 8 of 10 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** tool-vs-model-sorter
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Evaluate
**Bloom Verb:** judge
**Learning Objective:** The learner will judge whether each of ten rubric checks should be done by a tool, by the model, or by a person, with at least 8 of 10 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Tool Use, AI Agent, Large Language Model (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each check the learner commits one of three bins. A placement is correct when it matches the Correct bin column in Content. Mastery is at least 8 of 10 correct on the first attempt. Reading the division rule is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A model can count and measure reliably. (2) A tool can judge whether alt text is useful. (3) A model can confirm facts without a source. **Instructional Rationale:** Judging who should do a check is an Evaluate-level action that applies the division rule. Ten checks drawn from the rubric, with four for tools, four for the model, and two for a person, teach the learner to match the task to the right worker. **Content:** The division rule, shown at all times: tools do exact tasks like counting, measuring, testing, and comparing; the model does judgment tasks on text; a person does tasks that need a real source or a real-world test. The three bins: Tool, Model, Person. The ten checks: | # | Check shown to the learner | Correct bin | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | Count the images that have no alt attribute. | Tool | Counting is exact work. | | 2 | Measure the reading level of three passages. | Tool | A readability formula is a calculation. | | 3 | Test whether each link returns an error. | Tool | Testing a link is a repeatable test. | | 4 | Judge whether a piece of alt text is useful. | Model | It is a judgment about text, and a person should spot-check it. | | 5 | Decide whether a heading describes its section. | Model | It is a judgment about text. | | 6 | Decide whether a quiz feedback message explains why. | Model | It is a judgment about text. | | 7 | Test whether the resource embeds on a particular LMS. | Person | It needs a real test on a real platform. | | 8 | Compare the license on the page with the license in the metadata. | Tool | A comparison of two values is exact. | | 9 | Decide whether a learning outcome uses a measurable verb. | Model | It is a judgment about text. | | 10 | Confirm that a statistic in the resource matches its cited source. | Person | It needs the real source, and a person must open it. | **Provenance:** The checks are drawn from Chapters 5 to 10, and the sim labels the sorting "illustrative". The division rule follows the chapter section "Tool Use". **Rules:** Each check has exactly one correct bin. Four checks are Tool, four are Model, and two are Person. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one check and the three bins. 2. The learner places the check in a bin, and the placement is committed. 3. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text. 4. After check 10 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 10 checks in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [bin]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. This is for a [bin]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 10 correct on the first attempt". At 8 or more it adds "You can divide the work well." Below 8 it lists the Why text of each missed check. **Starting State:** The first check, the division rule, and three empty bins. The question shown is "Who should do this check?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter says exact tasks go to tools, judgment tasks go to the model, and real-world tasks stay with a person.
